##### **1.5 Gauss-Jordan Row Operations and Tableau Pivoting Mechanics** The transition from a current basic feasible solution to an adjacent improved basic feasible solution is executed algebraically through **pivoting**, an algorithmic sequence of **Gauss-Jordan elementary row operations**. Pivoting updates the linear constraint system and the objective relation so that the newly admitted basic variable assumes canonical identity-column form while the leaving variable recedes to nonbasic status. The mechanics of pivoting center on three structural coordinates: * **Pivot Column:** The column belonging to the entering variable, determined by the simplex optimality criterion. * **Pivot Row:** The constraint row corresponding to the leaving variable, determined by the minimum ratio test of the feasibility condition. * **Pivot Element:** The scalar located at the exact intersection of the pivot row and the pivot column. ```{mermaid} %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'Helvetica', 'primaryColor': '#e8f4f8', 'primaryTextColor': '#1f2d3d', 'primaryBorderColor': '#355c7d', 'lineColor': '#355c7d', 'secondaryColor': '#d6eef5', 'tertiaryColor': '#fff3cd', 'background': '#ffffff', 'mainBkg': '#e8f4f8', 'secondBkg': '#d6eef5', 'tertiaryBkg': '#fff3cd', 'clusterBkg': '#f9fbfd', 'clusterBorder': '#355c7d', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff' }}}%% %%| fig-cap: "Algorithmic flow of Gauss-Jordan tableau pivoting across an iteration" %%| fig-width: 7 %%| fig-height: 4 flowchart TB A["Identify entering and leaving variables
Locate pivot element at intersection"] --> B["Basis update
Swap leaving label for entering label"] B --> C["Normalize pivot row
Divide entire row by pivot element"] C --> D["Eliminate non-pivot constraint rows
Subtract scaled pivot row"] C --> E["Eliminate objective z-row
Subtract scaled pivot row"] D --> F["Preserved canonical form
Basic columns form identity matrix"] E --> F ``` The transformation to the next tableau proceeds through two sequential steps: 1. **Basis Update and Pivot Row Normalization:** In the **Basic** column of the tableau, replace the label of the leaving variable with the entering variable. The new pivot row is computed by dividing every entry in the current pivot row by the pivot element: $$\text{New pivot row} = \frac{\text{Current pivot row}}{\text{Pivot element}}$$ This forces the coefficient of the entering variable in its own row to become $+1$. 2. **Elimination on All Non-Pivot Rows (Including the $z$-Row):** Every remaining row $i$ (each non-pivot constraint row and the objective $z$-row) must have a zero in the pivot column. This is achieved by subtracting an appropriately scaled multiple of the normalized pivot row: $$\text{New row}_i = (\text{Current row}_i) - (\text{Pivot column coefficient in row } i) \times (\text{New pivot row})$$ Applying these operations across all rows ensures the **canonical unit-vector form**: each basic variable has a coefficient of $+1$ in its designated basic row and $0$ in all other constraint rows as well as the $z$-row, allowing the basic variable values to be read directly from the right-hand side **Solution** column. * **Worked Illustration:** In the starting tableau of the Tatar-Paint problem, $x_1$ is selected as the entering variable (pivot column) and $s_1$ as the leaving variable (pivot row). The pivot element at their intersection is $6$. The current rows are: $$\begin{aligned} z\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 & -4 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\ s_1\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 4 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 24 \end{bmatrix} \\ s_2\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix} \\ s_3\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\ s_4\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}$$ Executing the Gauss-Jordan update rules: $$\begin{aligned} \text{New } x_1\text{-row} &= \frac{1}{6} \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 4 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 24 \end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{6} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{New } z\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 & -4 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} - (-5) \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{6} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{5}{6} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 20 \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{New } s_2\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix} - (1) \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{6} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{6} & 1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{New } s_3\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} - (-1) \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{6} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & \frac{5}{3} & \frac{1}{6} & 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \text{New } s_4\text{-row} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} - (0) \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{6} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}$$ The resulting column under $x_1$ across the rows $(z, x_1, s_2, s_3, s_4)^T$ is $[0, 1, 0, 0, 0]^T$, verifying that the new basic variable $x_1$ is converted into a standard unit basis vector with value $x_1 = 4$ and objective level $z = 20$.
